text: There are few things that may not be said, in some manner or other; either in a seeming confidence, or a genteel irony, or introduced with wit; and one great part of the knowledge of the world consists in knowing when and where to make use of these different manners.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XLV, to his son, London, July, 20, Old Style 1748
